commit_reviews.summary: Sound greenfield scaffolding for a TypeScript CLI static-site generator with conventional ts-jest config, committed lockfile, and dependency choices (commander, gray-matter, marked) that match the stated task.

problems: default templates in templates.ts duplicate the fallback markup in generator.ts creating drift risk
escaped quotes in template literal strings
no error handling for invalid templatesDir
commit_reviews.summary: Adds an optional Handlebars templating layer (--templates flag, TemplateEngine class) that cleanly extends the existing build/parse/generate pipeline while staying fully backward compatible.

Dependency additions (chokidar, ws, @types/ws) exactly match the Session 3 integration spec's tech directives and are placed correctly (types in devDependencies, transitive deps promoted out of dev as chokidar becomes a runtime dependency).

compounding_issues: Seed mismatch: the committed seed (root index.ts) is an unrelated Express Todo API; Session 1 ignored it and built the SSG greenfield, leaving dead, uncompilable seed code (imports express/sqlite3 with no package.json deps) orphaned at repo root for the rest of the story
Session 1 committed node_modules and dist/ into git (~5,172 files, ~978k insertions) with no .gitignore, so every later session churns thousands of dependency files and bloats each commit

The story was designed for 5 sessions (plugin refactor + incremental builds) but only 3 sessions of work occurred; Session 3 had to be split into two commits ('integration' + 'integration (continued)') after flaky integration tests, so the intended arc is truncated

Session 3's initial serve.ts shipped usePolling:true/interval:200 chokidar config and an incorrect close() ordering (watcher closed inside wss callback); both had to be corrected in the continuation commit
The Handlebars page template uses noEscape:true, disabling escaping for the body in the template path that the string-fallback path does escape
key_decisions: Greenfield module split (types/parser/generator/build/index) in Session 1, establishing clean seams that Sessions 2 and 3 built directly on (build.ts accepts BuildOptions reused by serve.ts)
Choosing Handlebars with a dual path in generator.ts: custom TemplateEngine when a templates/ dir exists, string-based fallback otherwise — preserved all 22 existing tests unchanged in Session 2
Session 3 integrated the dev server through the existing build() call for rebuilds rather than duplicating render logic, plus a testable ServerInstance contract (ready promise, close())
Using commander subcommands (build/serve) with native http + ws + chokidar, and a path-traversal guard on served file resolution
Continuation commit hardened test robustness (polling loops, 15-30s timeouts, awaitWriteFinish) instead of weakening assertions
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality rose steadily across the sessions with the greenfield build, the template-engine feature, and the dev-server integration, but the arc is truncated: Session 1 produced a clean layered core with 22 tests, Session 2 extended it cleanly to 44 tests while keeping backward compatibility, and Session 3 attempted the most complex piece (a 191-line live-reload server with a 285-line integration test) whose first pass shipped flaky timing tests and a misconfigured watcher — the continuation commit recognized and fixed those flakiness and shutdown-ordering bugs, and all 56 tests pass at the end. The main degradations are collateral rather than code-quality: the orphaned seed file, the node_modules-in-git bloat that grows monotonically, and the fact that the final two planned sessions (plugin refactor, incremental builds) never ran.
story_review.summary: A logical, well-layered greenfield-to-feature-to-integration progression with clean backward compatibility and self-corrected integration flakiness, undermined by a mismatched orphaned seed, node_modules committed to git, and a truncated 3-of-5-session arc.
